Correct option: (3) Republic.

The chapter names India as the ‘Republic of India’ and Brazil as the ‘Federative Republic of Brazil’, so both countries are republics. Its ‘Do you know ?’ box gives the detail that separates them: India has a federal PARLIAMENTARY republic type of government while Brazil has a federal PRESIDENTIAL one. So 'Presidential' describes Brazil alone rather than both, and neither country has a military or a communist government — Brazil's populist military government ended in 1985.
